title: Nodal geometric curve fibres are geometrically reduced
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-algebraic-closure], the base change $C_\Omega=C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is either empty or has every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of topological Krull dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and each closed point [def-weil-closed-points] of $C_\Omega$ is either smooth over $\Omega$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] or has completed local ring isomorphic as an $\Omega$-algebra to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Here completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and the formal power series ring is [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $C$ is geometrically reduced: for every field extension $L/k$, $C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Neither properness, separatedness, connectedness nor a marking is required.

source.place: Tag 0E37 (lemma-facts-about-nodal-curves), lines 4546--4576, geometric reducedness assertion and proof; Tag 0C47 (definition-nodal), lines 3796--3808, and the completed-geometric-local-ring description immediately preceding it.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ and write $X=C_\Omega$. If $X$ is empty it is reduced. The structure morphism of $X$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. Choose a finite affine cover $C=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], its inverse images form the finite affine cover $X=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}(B_i\otimes_k\Omega)$. Thus $X$ is quasi-compact and its structure morphism is of finite type. The field $\Omega$ is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. The Jacobson statement [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] gives a closed specialization of every point, by applying its density assertion to the nonempty closed set which is that point's closure.

source.place: Tags 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type) and 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); varieties.tex Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson); schemes.tex Tags 01I4 and 01JR for the finite affine cover.

proof.text: Let $x$ be a closed point of $X$ which is smooth over $\Omega$. Smoothness is an open condition, so a neighbourhood of $x$ is smooth over $\Omega$; [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] says that this smooth morphism has geometrically reduced fibres, hence its local ring at $x$ is reduced. If instead the completed local ring at $x$ is $R=\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, then $R$ is reduced: restriction to the two axes gives an injection $R\hookrightarrow\Omega[[u]]\times\Omega[[v]]$, because a series vanishing on both axes is divisible by $uv$, and both factors are domains by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain]. The local ring $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Noetherian by step 1, and its completion $A\to\widehat A$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] and injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], applied with the zero ideal. A nilpotent of $A$ would map to a nilpotent of the reduced ring $R\cong\widehat A$, so it is zero; thus $A$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 0E37, proof of geometric reducedness: smooth completed local rings and the model \Omega[[u,v]]/(uv); algebra.tex Tags 00MC and 05CK for completion and injectivity.

proof.text: For an arbitrary point $y\in X$, choose a closed point $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$ using the Jacobson statement in step 1. The map $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{X,y}$ is a localization (because $y$ is a generization of $x$), so the reducedness of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ from step 2 implies the reducedness of $\mathcal O_{X,y}$. Hence every local ring of $X$ is reduced, and $X$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Thus $C_\Omega$ is reduced for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$.

source.place: Tag 0E37, conclusion from reduced completed local rings to reducedness of the nodal curve

proof.text: It remains to descend this conclusion to every field extension. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an affine chart of $C$ and let $E/k$ be finite purely inseparable. Choose an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ containing an embedding of $E$. The map $A\otimes_kE\to A\otimes_k\Omega$ is injective because $A$ is a flat $k$-module and tensoring the injection $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ over $k$ with $A$ preserves injectivity [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat, lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. By step 3 the target is reduced, so $A\otimes_kE$ is reduced. Applying [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-finite-inseparable-test] gives that $A\otimes_kL$ is reduced for every field extension $L/k$.

source.place: Tag 030V, finite purely inseparable test for geometric reducedness; curves.tex Tag 0E37

proof.text: For every $L/k$, the inverse images of the finite affine cover of $C$ are the open subschemes $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kL)$: this is [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] together with [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Each is reduced by step 4, so the local-ring characterization [def-pc-reduced-scheme] shows that $C_L$ is reduced. Since $L$ was arbitrary, $C$ is geometrically reduced.
